title: Social thinking of Arthur de Gobineau

photo.caption: Völker Europas, wahrt eure heiligsten Güter ("Peoples of Europe, guard your dearest goods," 1895) The Yellow Peril painting. Much of the imagery appears drawn from Gobineau's anti-Asian writings, via his friend Prince Philip von Eulenburg who helped with turning Wilhelm II's sketch into the painting.
photo.alt: A reproduction of the print entitled Völker Europas, wahrt eure heiligsten Güter ("Peoples of Europe, guard your dearest goods," 1895) or The Yellow Peril painting with an armed angel showing armed women a fiery battle.
